sections.normalized_html: Find [MATH: \dfrac{3}{7} - \left( -\dfrac{11}{7} \right).]
sections.readable_text: Find [MATH: \dfrac{3}{7} - \left( -\dfrac{11}{7} \right).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To subtract [MATH: -\dfrac{11}{7}] from [MATH: \dfrac{3}{7},] we combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives [MATH: (3)/(7) − (− (11)/(7))|= (3)/(7) + (11)/(7).]

We have a common denominator of [MATH: 7,] so we combine numerators: [MATH: (3)/(7) + (11)/(7) = (3 + 11)/(7) = (14)/(7)]

Now, we can simplify the resulting fraction: [MATH: (14)/(7)|= 14 ÷ 7 = 2]

Note: If two fractions have different denominators, we need to put them over a common denominator first and then add or subtract!

To subtract [MATH: -\dfrac{11}{7}] from [MATH: \dfrac{3}{7},] we combine the two negative signs to make a single plus sign. This gives
[MATH: (3)/(7) − (− (11)/(7))|= (3)/(7) + (11)/(7).]

We have a common denominator of [MATH: 7,] so we combine numerators:
[MATH: (3)/(7) + (11)/(7) = (3 + 11)/(7) = (14)/(7)]

Now, we can simplify the resulting fraction:
[MATH: (14)/(7)|= 14 ÷ 7 = 2]

Note: If two fractions have different denominators, we need to put them over a common denominator first and then add or subtract!
